Let independent product inputs have $X_1\sim\operatorname{Bern}(p)$ and $X_2\sim\operatorname{Bern}(q)$. Since $Y=X_1+X_2$ is deterministic, expansion of [F3] gives $I(X_1,X_2;Y)=H(Y)$. Put $A=2p-1$, $B=2q-1$, and $T=AB$. Then
$$P_Y(0)=\frac{(1-A)(1-B)}4,\quad P_Y(1)=\frac{1-T}2,\quad P_Y(2)=\frac{(1+A)(1+B)}4.$$
The two endpoint masses sum to $(1+T)/2$, and their difference has absolute value $|A+B|/2$.

If $T\le0$, equal endpoint masses are feasible by taking $B=-A$ and $A^2=-T$. At fixed middle mass, entropy is maximized when the endpoint masses are equal because binary entropy is maximized at one half. Thus, with $b=P_Y(1)\ge1/2$,
$$H(Y)\le h_b(b)+(1-b)\ln2,$$
where $h_b(b)=-b\ln b-(1-b)\ln(1-b)$. Its derivative is $\ln((1-b)/b)-\ln2<0$ for $b\ge1/2$, so this is at most its value $\frac32\ln2$ at $b=1/2$.
